The lender is trusted to claim that his prozbul was lost, as mentioned in the previous halachah, and we do not suspect that the loan was after the writing of the prozbul that was lost; if so, he is surely trusted regarding a prozbul in his possession that it was written after the loan.
it is not released, for I did not convert it into a loan. As above, halachah 11.

it is a presumption etc.. Since a person has the possibility of receiving his money permissibly, we assume that he would prefer this option to a false claim that the debt is shop credit, and therefore he is trusted in his claim.

and he handed his words over to the students. That for Torah scholars they were lenient that they do not need a distinguished court (Rikevo, Orah V'Simchah), since the need for a distinguished court is so that the release of monies in our time not be treated lightly, and with Torah scholars there is no such concern (Yad Peshutah). Some explain that this refers to students who are judges in a distinguished court of the generation, like the court of Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, as above, halachah 17 (Kesef Mishneh).
anyone who returns etc.. Even when the lender did not make a prozbul, or at a time when the shemitah year applies by Torah law and a prozbul is of no help (as above, halakhah 16).
the spirit of the Sages is pleased with him. The Sages are pleased with the act he did beyond the letter of the law.
and he did not say this to him. The borrower did not say that he was giving it as a gift.
he should hint to him with words. He hints to him.
rather he should take his money and go. The borrower should go on his way, with the money remaining in his hand.
lest he delay etc.. Lest the borrower not repay the debt until the time of the cancellation of monetary debts.
two negative commandments. Two prohibitions.
as it is said, "Beware lest there be". "Beware" is one negative commandment, and "lest" is a second.
and to sanctify the fiftieth year. To proclaim it a holy year, in which one must refrain from working the land and declare the produce ownerless (see also Sefer HaMitzvot, positive commandment 136).
and from when did they begin to count. Shemitah years and jubilees.
after fourteen years from when they entered the land. After the end of fourteen years from the time they entered the land under Joshua.

six years you shall sow your field etc.. Shemitah years and jubilees are counted only from the time that every field is assigned to a particular person, and this situation existed only after the conquest of the land and the division of the inheritances.

you find that you say etc.. The days of creation until the creation of man are counted as the first year of the world's creation, and the day man was created is Rosh Hashanah of the second year of creation. The Exodus from Egypt was in the year 2448 from the creation of man (as follows from Seder Olam Rabbah; see also Babylonian Talmud, Avodah Zarah 9a and Rashi there), and after it 40 years passed in the wilderness and another 14 years in conquering and dividing the land. It turns out that the first year of the count was the year 2503 from the creation of man, which is the year 2504 from the creation of the world, and therefore the year 2510 from creation was a shemitah year.
and they made the year five hundred and ten of creation. The year 510 of the third thousand of creation, that is, the year 2510.

seventeen jubilees... and it was the thirty-sixth year of the jubilee. From the entry into the land until the destruction of the First Temple, sixteen complete jubilees were counted, and in the thirty-sixth year of the seventeenth jubilee they went into exile (and when the fourteen years of conquest and division are also counted, it turns out that they made seventeen complete jubilees - Responsa of the Rambam, Shafat).
and the year in which they left. In which they went into exile from the land.

the year in which the Temple was destroyed the first time was the year after a shemitah year. The first year after the destruction of the First Temple was the year following a shemitah, since the Temple was destroyed at the end of a shemitah year (Responsa of the Rambam, Shafat, just as happened with the Second Temple, as below, halakhah 4 - Yad Peshutah).
since the land ceased. Since settlement of the land ceased.

and this is the second entry. The first entry was by those who came up from Egypt, and then the land was sanctified with the first sanctity, which was nullified at the time of the exile; with the second entry, by those who came up from Babylonia, the land was sanctified with a second sanctity forever (Hilchot Terumot 1:5).
for there was no jubilee in the Second Temple period. For the jubilee applies only when all of Israel is on its land, as below, halakhah 8.
in order to sanctify the shemitah years. In order to know when a shemitah year is, since the jubilee year interrupts the fixed count of seven after seven, as below, halakhah 7.

for the year in which the Temple was destroyed the last time, which began from Tishrei, two months after the destruction. The year that began two months after the destruction of the Second Temple (this year is called the year of the destruction, since from the month of Nisan before the destruction until the month of Nisan after it is called the year of the destruction, in contrast to shemitah, which begins in Tishrei - Pe'at HaShulchan 29:6).

to the count of documents. To the reign of Alexander of Macedon (Hilchot Gerushin 1:27), a count that was in use in the days of the Sages and the Geonim, and which began in the year 3450 from the creation of the world, 311 years before the common era.
which is the year four thousand nine hundred thirty-six of creation. The year 1176 of the common era.
the Geonim. The Sages of the generations after the Talmud.

that they did not count etc.. In the opinion of the Geonim, in the time of the destruction the years are counted seven after seven without interruption, and only in the time of the First and Second Temples did the jubilee interrupt in between, in contrast to the calculation brought in the previous halakhot, according to which a jubilee year interrupts the count of the sevens even in the time of the destruction.
from the Talmud of Avodah Zarah. From the Gemara in tractate Avodah Zarah (page 9b).
according to this calculation, which is a tradition. According to the calculation based on the tradition of the Geonim.

and they all counted only from the years of the destruction. The count is based on the fact that the first year after the destruction of the Second Temple was the year after a shemitah (as above, halakhah 4), which is the first year in the count of the next shemitah, and after that they counted seven after seven without interruption.
cast them off by sevens. Divide the years since the destruction into sevens.

let this year, which is the year one thousand one hundred and seven from the destruction, be the year after a shemitah. For the year before it is the year 1106 from the destruction of the Second Temple, and this number is a multiple of seven.
and the practice. The accepted custom.

the jubilee year is not counted in the count of the two sevens. The jubilee year is not counted as part of the seven-year cycle, but comes after the shemitah year, and after it a new shemitah cycle begins (and this law applied until the destruction of the First Temple and in the Second Temple period, when shemitahs and jubilees were counted, and it will apply again when they begin once more to count shemitahs and jubilees, as explained below, 12:16).
the beginning of the six years of a seven-year cycle. The first year in the count of the next shemitah.
from when the tribe of Reuben went into exile etc.. Before the destruction of the First Temple (see I Chronicles 5:26).
when all its inhabitants are on it. When all the tribes of Israel are in the Land of Israel.
all of them dwelling as is proper. Each tribe in its own inheritance.
applies outside the Land. With regard to freeing slaves (but not the laws connected to land, explained below, and not the blowing of the shofar - Aruch HaShulchan 30:15; see below, halakhah 10).
even not in the presence of the Temple. The jubilee applies when all its inhabitants are on it, even if the Temple is not standing.
the law of the Hebrew slave applies. A Jew can be sold into slavery, as explained in Hilchot Avadim 1:1.
and the law of houses in walled cities. Special laws of sale that apply to houses in a walled city, as explained below, chapter 12.

and the law of a devoted field. If a person said of his field in the Land of Israel, "This is devoted," it is given to the priests who serve in the Temple at that time (Hilchot Arachin VaCharamin 6:5). But at a time when the jubilee does not apply, his words have no effect (ibid. 8:11).
and the law of an inherited field. The laws of sale and consecration of a field that a person received as an inheritance (as explained in Hilchot Arachin VaCharamin, chapter 4).

and we accept a resident alien. A gentile who accepted upon himself the Noahide commandments because of the command of the Holy One, blessed be He, and who wishes to live in the Land of Israel (Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah 14:7, Hilchot Melachim 8:11).

and shemitah applies in the Land by rabbinic law etc.. All the laws of shemitah that apply in the Land of Israel, as well as the law of the cancellation of monetary debts that applies everywhere, are not obligations from the Torah but from the words of the Sages.
as we have explained. Above 9:2-3, regarding the cancellation of monetary debts.
on the tenth of Tishrei. Yom Kippur.
is entrusted first to the court. That they blow first.
and they blow the shofar nine times, in the manner in which they blow on Rosh Hashanah. Tekiah, teruah, tekiah, three times (Hilchot Shofar 3:1).
and they pass the shofar throughout the entire border of Israel. They blow everywhere throughout the land, but not outside the Land (Aruch HaShulchan 31:4, Devar Avraham).

11-12. it is the same for everything. On these two occasions they blow the curved horn of a ram (Hilchot Shofar 1:1), and both are equal in all the laws of the shofar detailed in Hilchot Shofar, chapter 1.
and the jubilee and Rosh Hashanah are the same for the blasts. Both are equal with regard to the number and laws of the blasts, such as the laws detailed in Hilchot Shofar 3:4-5.

except that on the jubilee they blow etc.. There is a difference between blowing for the jubilee and blowing on Rosh Hashanah regarding blowing on Shabbat: when Rosh Hashanah falls on Shabbat, the Sages decreed that one may blow only in the presence of a court that has authority to sanctify months and that fixed there when Rosh Hashanah would fall (Hilchot Shofar 2:6-9), whereas for the jubilee blast they did not make this decree, even though Yom Kippur is forbidden for all labors like Shabbat. However, even for the jubilee blast they ordained that one should not blow throughout the land except during the hours when the judges are in the court.

three things are indispensable for the jubilee. That if they did not do one of these, the year is not sanctified and the prohibitions of the Land's rest do not apply in it (Rashi and Tosafot, Rosh Hashanah 9b; and see Aruch HaShulchan 31:5, who brought another explanation).
and the release of slaves. Hebrew slaves.
and the return of fields to their owners. As explained below, chapter 11.
and their crowns on their heads. They cover their heads with a dignified head covering as a sign of freedom.
and releases land etc.. That land that was sold returns to its owners in the jubilee, as explained in the next chapter.
as we have explained. Above 9:4.
permanently. Forever.
both of them. The seller and the buyer.
his ancestral field. The inheritance of his forefathers.

and if he transgressed and sold in any case... and we judge the house etc.. If he sold a house or his ancestral field nevertheless, not for the sake of sustenance, the sale stands, and they are treated like any house or field that is sold, to which the laws detailed in this chapter and the next chapter apply.
to calculate the money. To assess the value of the field.
and whenever he wishes to redeem. To buy it back, even if the buyer is not interested.
he calculates with the buyer for the years that he ate. They make a calculation according to the number of years that the field was in the buyer's possession and he ate its produce.
if there remained ten years until the jubilee. The sale took place ten years before the jubilee.
and he sold him his field for a hundred dinars. Accordingly, the value of each year is ten dinars.
and the fruit of a sycamore. The beams and branches of the sycamore.
they belong to the buyer, like the rest of its fruit. They are treated as fruit even though they are not eaten.
that was cut down. That was chopped down.

both of them are forbidden to use it. The seller is forbidden to use the wood, for burning and the like, because the land and everything in it is in the buyer's possession. And the buyer is forbidden, because wood sold together with the land is treated as land that returns to its owner.
it is sold and land is bought with its proceeds. They sell the wood and buy land in its place.

until the field is redeemed from his hand. If the seller obtains money and redeems the field from the buyer before the jubilee, he can benefit from the produce growing in the land that was bought with the proceeds of the dry wood, until this land returns to its owner in the jubilee (Mirkevet HaMishneh).
they assess the improvement of the trees in it. They assess the rise in the field's value resulting from the planting of the trees.
as we have explained. Above 10:9.
it is not permitted to redeem for less than two years. The seller may buy it back only after two years have passed from the time of the sale.
by number of years after the jubilee you shall buy. From this it follows that an obligation rests on the buyer as well that the purchase of the field be for "a number of years."
from time to time. From the date of sale until this date two years later.
two crops. A crop of two years.
blight. A drying disease of the grain.

mildew. It seems this is a result of the blight, in which the ears take on a greenish-yellow appearance, causing the ears to sprout early before the kernels ripen (see Da'at Mikra, Amos 4:9; Sperber, Ta'anit 3:5).
fallow. Uncultivated.
and plowed it. He plowed it.
if he sold it one year before the jubilee. A year that counts in the count (for the shemitah before the jubilee is not part of the count, as above, halakhah 10).

the buyer eats it the second year after the jubilee. The buyer holds the land for one year after the jubilee to complete two years, and afterward returns it to the seller, since the jubilee canceled his right.
pits. Holes.
for less than two years. Before two years have passed since the sale.
returns to the owners in the jubilee. For such land too is considered an inherited field.
he sold trees. Without the land (Radbaz; compare above, halakhah 7).
for they are fit for crops. They produce yield. And barren trees are redeemed immediately (Radbaz).

he calculates only with the first one. The calculation of the amount the owner must give in order to redeem (as explained above, halakhot 4 and 5) is made according to the amount he received from the first buyer.
and it lost value. Its value decreased.
according to what it is. According to its value now.
they always favor the seller of an inherited field. Since he was forced to sell his ancestral field because of financial hardship (Commentary on the Mishnah, Arachin 9:2).
17-18. they do not listen to him. He is not permitted to redeem his field except with the buyer's consent (Commentary on the Mishnah, Arachin 9:2).
and if his relatives wished to redeem, they redeem. Against the buyer's will.
his relatives. On his father's side, who are fit to inherit from him (Devar Avraham).

or his uncle or his uncle's son shall redeem him. This was said regarding one who sold himself to a gentile, and from there it is learned for the other redemptions that all relatives may redeem (Yad Peshutah).
brothers who divided. Who divided between themselves their father's estate that they received as an inheritance.
they are like purchasers. Each of them is considered to have bought his portion from the other.

and they return... and their portion shall not be annulled from what it was. They do not need to make a new division, but only to exchange portions between them until the next jubilee (Rik"v, Kesef Mishneh, and Aruch HaShulchan 32:13; and see another explanation in Piskei VeShitot).
the firstborn. Who inherits a double portion.
and one who performs levirate marriage with his brother's wife. One who marries the wife of his brother who died without children, who also receives a double portion (Hilchot Nachalot 3:7).
returns in the jubilee etc.. He gives his brothers his double portion, and receives from them another double portion.
even though a husband's inheritance is rabbinic. The Sages enacted that a husband inherits his wife (Hilchot Ishut 12:3).

they gave strength to their words like that of the Torah, and he does not return in the jubilee. The Sages gave a husband's inheritance the force of inheritance by Torah law, which does not return in the jubilee.

he returns it to the members of the family because of a family disgrace. He returns it to his wife's family, since her family members were buried there, and if the place left their possession it would be considered a disgrace.
and they give him its price etc.. They pay him the price of the burial plot, except for the price of his wife's grave.
for he is obligated to bury her. And he must bear the expenses involved (ibid. 14:23-24).
for every twelve months from the day he sold. Until the date of the sale arrives again after a year.
and he may sell some of his property and redeem. He is permitted to do so (and compare the law of an inherited field above, 11:17-18).
we count for the first one. We count twelve months from the day of the sale for the first buyer.
the house became absolutely the second one's. The second buyer's purchase becomes final, and the house cannot be redeemed from him.

for the seller sold to the second any right that would come into his hand. The first buyer sold to the second buyer all his rights in the house, and therefore the house became final in the second one's hand after a year from the day of the sale to the first.

if the buyer went down in the month of intercalation. The month of intercalation is the first Adar, which is the month added to the year. A buyer in this month gets additional time, so his year ends after that of one who bought at the beginning of the second Adar.
the day of the twelfth month. The last day of the year.
and breaks the door and enters his house. The Sages permitted the seller to do this, since buyers used to hide at the end of the year (Mishnah, Arachin 9:4).
one who consecrates. To the Temple's property.
and another redeemed it from the hand of the Temple treasury. Another person bought the house from the Temple treasury.

for the Temple treasury does not make final, only the purchase. A house in a walled city that was consecrated can always be redeemed, and therefore the year is counted from the time of the purchase ("the purchase") from the Temple treasury.
to the one who bought it, throughout his generations. To a buyer who has heirs, and not to the Temple treasury.
in the houses of the courtyards. In a city that is not surrounded by a wall.
in a city that is not properly walled. As below, halakhot 14-15.

this is redeemed with the better power etc.. According to the conditions of redemption that favor the seller and treat him well in the law of an inherited field, and also according to these conditions of redemption in the law of houses in walled cities, so it turns out that there is no limit on the time of its redemption.
if he wished to redeem immediately, he redeems, as in the law of houses. In contrast to an inherited field, which cannot be redeemed in less than two years.
he calculates with the seller and deducts from him what he ate. The seller returns to the buyer his money, minus the time the buyer used the house, as explained above, 11:4-5.

gardens... fields. Gardens are plantings of trees, and fields are areas for sowing (Me'iri HaKatzar, Tosafot Yom Tov and Rash Sirilio on Ma'aserot 3:10; and Devar Avraham wrote that beds of vegetables are also included in gardens).
like the law of fields outside the city. Like the law of an inherited field explained above, chapter 11.

a house that does not have etc.. Since it is not fit for use as a house (in contrast to the dovecotes above, halakhah 11, which are fit for their use even though they lack four by four cubits - Yad Peshutah).
it is not made final among houses of walled cities. Its law is that of an inherited field (Rik"v).

and in Jerusalem a house is not made final. Because it was not divided among the tribes and there is no private ownership in it (Hilchot Beit HaBechirah 7:14). And the law of houses in Jerusalem is like the law of houses of courtyards (Rik"v).

and a house built into the wall etc.. A house whose outer wall is part of the city wall is not considered surrounded by a wall, since it has no further wall outside its outer wall (Aruch HaShulchan 34:16).
a city whose roofs are its wall. The outer houses in it are built adjacent to one another and form a kind of wall.
that was settled. In which dwelling houses were built.
even though it is walled now. At the time of the sale of the house (and the discussion here concerns the time before the first destruction - Kesef Mishneh and Radbaz).
the sanctity of the houses of walled cities. With regard to the special laws of sale, as well as other laws that apply in walled cities (see Hilchot Beit HaBechirah 7:13).
in the second entry. The going up to the Land after the Babylonian exile.

they also counted their entry in the days of Ezra... and they sanctified etc.. Ezra sanctified the land so that all Israel would come and all the laws from the Torah would apply. In the end, however, the laws from the Torah did not apply (see above 10:3 regarding the jubilee, above 10:9 regarding houses of walled cities, Hilchot Terumot 1:26 regarding the tithe).
and their open land. The outskirts of the city.
the six cities of refuge. Which take in an unintentional killer (Hilchot Rotzei'ach 5:1).
and in addition to them. And besides.
forty-two cities. See there 8:9-10.
and when they add other cities of refuge in the days of the Messiah. See there 8:4.
the first thousand. A thousand cubits adjacent to the city on every side.
open land. Outer neighborhoods in which shepherds and farmers live (Commentary on the Mishnah, Arachin 9:8).
and from the oral tradition. The tradition of the Sages in explaining the verses.
and he shall not plant his ruin as a garden. So that he will not despair of rebuilding it.
in this order. Which was explained above, chapters 11-12.
and they redeem immediately. They redeem an inherited field even in the first two years.

and if they consecrated a field, they redeem from the Temple treasury after the jubilee. In contrast to an Israelite who consecrated a field: if he did not redeem it by the jubilee, the priests redeem it for themselves (Hilchot Arachin VaCharamin 4:19).

for it was not said "an eternal redemption shall be for the Levites" except in the cities of the Levites. The meaning of the verse "for the Levites" is the cities of the Levites and not the members of the tribe of Levi.

they do not wage war like Israel, nor inherit, nor acquire for themselves by the strength of their bodies. The war of the Levites is not like the war of Israel, who fight in order to inherit and take spoils ("acquire for themselves"), but the Levites participate in war as part of all of Israel (Yad Peshutah, since the previous halakhot imply that the Levites participate in war, and so it emerges from Hilchot Melachim 7:8, 7:10, 8:4. And see Devar Avraham, who explained differently).
